video.title: I Mixed GPT-6 Astra with Higgsfield - It’s INSANE

summary: George McConnell demonstrates a workflow inside ChatGPT (called 'GPT-6 Astra') using the Higgsfield plugin to produce a full ad campaign for a pink iPhone case: a 30-second video ad, a 16:9 cinematic ad, five static stills, a reusable named AI model ('Victoria'), UGC-style photos, and UGC talking videos with hook variations. Takeaway: product ad creative (video, stills, AI influencer UGC) can be produced from a product photo and prompts in minutes, and the creator's tip is to post 3-5 versions with different hooks on TikTok then move the winner to Instagram/Facebook. It is a tool demo with no revenue or business numbers, and it promotes the Higgsfield plugin via affiliate-style links.

speakers.name: George McConnell
speakers.description: YouTube creator demonstrating AI ad tools for product sellers

ideas.name: AI-generated product ad campaigns and UGC for physical product sellers
ideas.one_liner: Use ChatGPT plus the Higgsfield plugin to turn a product photo into video ads, stills and AI-influencer UGC for ecommerce brands.
ideas.business_model: Not stated; demonstrated as a workflow for sellers of cases, mugs and wall art. Could be run as an in-house marketing method or sold as a creative service (e.g. per-campaign or retainer).
ideas.customer: Sellers of physical products such as phone cases, mugs and wall art
ideas.problem: Producing product ads, consistent model imagery and UGC-style videos is slow and expensive.
ideas.offer: A full ad campaign from a product photo: 30s video spot, 16:9 director-style ad, five 4:5 stills, a locked reusable AI character, UGC photos and 20s UGC talking videos with hook variants.

pricing.notes: No pricing for any service; only mention is that the host is on a lower Higgsfield plan and hit rate limits.

acquisition_channels.details: Post 3-5 versions of the same UGC video with different hooks (question, hot take, product theme) on TikTok, then put the winner on Instagram and Facebook. Stills also pushed on Facebook, Instagram and email.

quote.text: they just launch three to five of the same exact video with different hooks on Tik Tok and then they put the winner on Instagram and Facebook
quote.speaker: George McConnell

acquisition_channels.details: Ads and stills intended to be pushed to people on Facebook and Instagram; a 16:9 ad for YouTube.

ideas.delivery: Done in a ChatGPT chat window: prompts call the Higgsfield plugin, which routes to video/image models (Cling, Seedance 2.5, Veo 3 mentioned). Generation takes about 40 seconds to 5 minutes per asset. Character is defined by a detailed prompt, named, then reused by name. Outputs are also viewable in the Higgsfield library.
unit_economics_claims: Five stills from a video took about 5 minutes
Character image generated in about 1 minute 6 seconds
ideas.startup_cost: not stated (requires ChatGPT and Higgsfield plans; credits used)

acquisition.how: Content and ad creative can be generated and posted by agents; posting and hook testing on TikTok/IG/FB is inbound and automatable, with human checks on performance.

onboarding.how: Customer only needs to supply a product photo and brief; an agent can collect these and set up the character prompt.

delivery.how: Generation is prompt-driven and fast, but outputs needed regeneration (model quirks, unrealistic scenes, NSFW false flag, messy kitchen) so a human reviews quality.

billing.how: Standard invoicing/subscription tools; nothing specific stated.

support.how: Revisions are further prompts; an agent can handle most with human review of quality.

uk_applicability.notes: Tools and platforms work in the UK. Need to follow ASA/CAP rules on disclosing AI-generated influencers and not implying fake real-customer testimonials; UGC-style fake reviews could breach consumer protection rules (CMA/DMCC).

risks: Plugin rate limits blocked 3 of 5 video generations on a lower plan
Safety filter falsely flagged a prompt as not safe for work (credits refunded)
AI outputs can look fake or produce odd scenes (empty street, same outfit, over-messy kitchen)
Presenting AI UGC as real customers may breach advertising/consumer rules
Dependence on third-party model and plugin availability

tactics.name: Install Higgsfield plugin in ChatGPT and generate an ad from a product photo
steps: Install the Higgsfield plugin via the link, click add to plugin, log into ChatGPT, install and allow
Attach the product photo (background removal is automatic)
Prompt: make a high energy ad for the product using Higgsfield, with campaign name
Specify the video model (e.g. Seedance 2.5) if the default output is poor

quote.text: if you want something specific such as sea dance, cling, v3, whatever you want, make sure you type it in on the chat window
quote.speaker: George McConnell

tactics.name: Lock a reusable AI character
steps: Describe the persona (age, vibe, hair, makeup)
Ask ChatGPT with Higgsfield to write a detailed identity prompt covering bone structure, eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, teeth
Rename the character and reuse by name
Attach product reference and instruct not to alter face, hair or build

tactics.name: Make AI stills look like real UGC
steps: Then ask for more realistic natural photos with different clothing in each, phone camera quality, slightly imperfect framing, real room clutter
Apply this request after generation rather than before to avoid confusing the model

tactics.name: Hook-variant testing across platforms
steps: Generate a 20s UGC video, choose the best
Request three alternative openers for the first two seconds (question, hot take, product theme)
Move the winning video to Instagram and Facebook

tactics.name: Recover from safety-filter false flag
steps: If a prompt is flagged not safe for work, credits are refunded
Rerun adding context about what people are wearing

warnings.warning: AI images may look obviously AI (empty streets, same outfit) and need realism prompting.
Cling does poorly with short prompts and produced a static image with an odd overlay.

lessons.lesson: Name a reusable AI character and attach the product reference every time to keep identity and product consistent across assets.
Ask for realism fixes (clutter, imperfect framing, varied outfits) after the first generation to make AI imagery pass as UGC.
Test several hooks on one platform before pushing the winner to others; cheap AI generation makes this affordable.
Choose the video model per task; short prompts suit Seedance, longer detailed prompts suit director-style ads.
A single ad is not enough: shoppers who see an ad will look up the brand, so profile content with a face and lifestyle imagery matters.
Plan for rate limits and false content flags when building agent workflows on top of generation tools.

evidence_quality.rationale: Tool demo with no business results, revenue or customer data; claims such as how creators go viral are unverified, and the video relies on a new plugin and model.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes the Higgsfield plugin with links in the description and first comment, likely affiliate or sponsored.
